<reason>B turned every one of A's examples in the opening — superbloom, Maya Bay, Hallstatt, Gion all resolve through physical management or property rules, not promotion limits — and sustained a clean dilemma all debate: narrowed to destinations' own feeds the motion prevents none of the cited harms; given teeth via permits or platform compulsion it becomes a vague, reach-based speech license. A's aggregation mechanism won a concession but never evidence that suppressing pins protects places, and A's visible retreat from influencer permits to "the motion does not specify the instrument" fed B's unfalsifiability charge. A's additive "gates-plus" framing and prediction-asymmetry point kept it genuinely competitive, but B answered both pressure questions directly, punished A's non-answer to the demand for one prevented harm, and closed on the cleaner distinction: recruitment is not arrival, and only access controls meter capacity. Both had one clipped turn; costs roughly cancel.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's opening reversal — "Every remedy PRO just cited is our case" — forced A to argue from mechanism rather than example for the rest of the debate; it was sealed when B's Q1 asked for one cited harm the narrowed motion would have prevented and A could offer only a voluntary education campaign (Jackson Hole) and a property-based photography rule (Gion).</best_rebuttal>
